title: The Optimist
subtitle: Sam Altman, OpenAI, and the Race to Invent the Future
pitch: A Wall Street Journal reporter's biography of Sam Altman, from childhood in St. Louis to the boardroom crisis of 2023.

chapters.g: Opens in the middle of the drama around Altman and OpenAI.
Growing up, early interests and the world of early internet culture.
Stanford and the start of his tech career.
Leaving university to start a company.
His first startup, Loopt, a location sharing app.
The mixed lessons of Loopt's sale and his growing reputation.
Rising influence in Silicon Valley and beyond.
The founding of OpenAI as a nonprofit to build safe AGI.
The effective altruism and AI safety world around OpenAI.
Creating a capped profit company and the Microsoft deal.
The November 2023 firing and return, which staff called 'the blip'.
Altman after his return, and where OpenAI is headed.
Closing thoughts on the man and the race.

ideas: Understanding AI's future means understanding the people steering it.
OpenAI's structure changed from nonprofit to profit seeking.
Safety tensions shaped OpenAI's biggest crisis.

args.a: Altman's optimism and dealmaking shaped modern AI.
args.c: Some readers want more on the technical and safety stakes than a biography can give.

questions: What does Altman's story tell you about who gets to decide AI's future?
Did OpenAI's switch to profit change its safety culture?

quiz.q: What did OpenAI staff call the 2023 firing and return?
quiz.w: The chapter is titled The blip.
Loopt was a location sharing app.
